newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel steady on tight avails.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel steady on tight avails.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run was quiet by mid-week with sellers in the $102 to $105 range while high sulphur Russian material was offered steady on the back of tight avails.
Traders said two refiners were offering 0.5 to 0.7 pct sulphur straight-run at $102 and $103 respectively, a little lower than Tuesday for the former.
Only one buyer was heard on the market looking for 0.4 pct or less material and bidding a maximum of $101.

A trader was heard offering at $105 to a U.S. independent refiner looking for a cargo to add to three ones bought earlier for shipment to the United States, but traders said they did not believe a deal would be done at that level.
High sulphur straight-run continued to be offered steady after a cargo changed hands on Tuesday at two means plus $5.25.
Two M-100 cargoes were on offer at that level and E-4 was on offer at three means plus $6/$6.50.
"There's not a lot of Russian straight-run around, that's why that price was paid," one trader said.
A second trader, seconding that view, added: "I would not be surprised if something was done today at $6 (premium to two means)."
